cards.explanation: The answer is True. The expert in the law, a man who knows God's Law, asks his big question. Jesus hands one right back: “What is written in the Law?” (Luke 10:26). I think the man came to do the quizzing and suddenly he's the one with the pop quiz.

The two commands are about loving God and loving your neighbor. The expert says to love the Lord your God with everything you've got, and to “Love your neighbor as yourself.” Two commands, one about God and one about the person next to you. Hang onto that second one, friends, because the whole story is about to lean on it.

The answer is False. Jesus tells the expert, “You have answered correctly…” (Luke 10:28). He doesn't add anything or take anything away. The expert had the answer, and now the question is what he'll do with it.
The word is do. Jesus says, “Do this and you will live.” (Luke 10:28). Not just know it, not just say it, do it. I've memorized plenty of recipes in my day, and not one of them ever baked itself.
The expert asks, “And who is my neighbor?” The text says he wanted to justify himself (Luke 10:29). So the man who gave the right answer asks one more question. I think a lot of us know that feeling.

The priest passes by on the other side. The priest, a man who served in God's house, saw the man and “…passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:31). Jesus doesn't tell us why. He just tells us what the priest did, and I think that picture is enough.

The answer is False. Jesus says a Levite, a man from the tribe of Levi, came to that spot and saw the man, and “…he passed by on the other side.” (Luke 10:32). He keeps on walking, just like the priest before him (Luke 10:31). Two men came by, friends, and neither one stopped.

The Samaritan goes to the man and bandages his wounds. The Samaritan, a man from Samaria, has compassion, then “…went to him and bandaged his wounds…” (Luke 10:34). The compassion comes first, and then he goes to the man.
He puts the man on his own animal. The Samaritan “…put him on his own animal…” (Luke 10:34). It's his own animal, not somebody else's. I think that's a generous thing to share.

He brings him to an inn. The Samaritan puts the man on his animal and “…brought him to an inn…” (Luke 10:34). An inn is a place for travelers to stay. The road was no place to leave a man half dead, and the Samaritan didn't.

The answer is True. Jesus says the Samaritan “…took care of him.” (Luke 10:34). He didn't just drop the man off at the door. He stayed and looked after him, and the next day we see him paying the innkeeper.

He tells the innkeeper to take care of the man and promises to repay him. The Samaritan says, “Take care of him…” and “…on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.” (Luke 10:35). He pays two denarii up front and says he'll cover whatever else comes up. I think that innkeeper got a pretty easy customer.

The expert answers, “The one who showed him mercy…” (Luke 10:37). He never says the word Samaritan, but he points straight at the man who stopped. Remember, friends, he started out asking who his neighbor is. Now he's answering who acted like one.

Jesus tells him to go and do the same. His words are, “Go and do likewise.” (Luke 10:37). Go back to what Jesus said earlier: “Do this and you will live.” (Luke 10:28). The story ends with a job, not a test score.
